items.sourceSection: Search PubMed; Filters; Search by author; Last update
items.paraphrase: PubMed search guidance explains how to refine searches with specific terms, field tags, filters and citation details; a search result is not itself verification of a study's conclusions.

items.criticalLimit: Search-ranking, citation indexing and result counts do not prove a study is correct, accessible or suitable for a decision.

items.title: What's a transit?
items.documentVersion: NASA Science public explainer; specific revision date not asserted
items.paraphrase: A transiting exoplanet can cause a measurable dip in a star's observed brightness; the light curve and orbital period can inform estimates of the planet's properties.
items.application: Use as an example of observational inference and measurement limitations in JANEWAY's astronomy and discovery methods.
items.criticalLimit: A dip in one fictional light curve alone does not conclusively identify a planet or establish its size without controls and follow-up.

items.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
items.title: NIST Technical Note 1297: Guidelines for Evaluating and Expressing the Uncertainty of NIST Measurement Results
items.sourceSection: Classification of Components of Uncertainty; Combined Standard Uncertainty
items.paraphrase: NIST describes evaluating individual measurement uncertainty components and combining them when reporting a measurement result, rather than presenting estimates as perfectly exact.
items.application: Use as a suggested check on units, precision and reporting uncertainty when SEVEN prepares data or measurement summaries.
items.criticalLimit: This is measurement guidance, not a universal statistical model or proof that any supplied dataset has valid sampling assumptions.
